chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Suheym, from Ibn Abu Yafour, who said:
I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying while he was raising his hand towards the sky: 'O Lord! Do not leave me to myself for the blink of an eye, ever, neither less than that nor more.'

He said, 'So it was with immediate flow of the tears from the sides of his beard. Then he turned towards me and said: O Ibn Abu Yafour! Yunus ibn Matta, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, left him to himself for less than the blink of an eye, so he committed that sin.' I said, 'So did he reach disbelief with it, may Allah keep you well?' He said: 'No, but death upon that state is destruction.'

key_terms.إِلَى نَفْسِي: To myself / To my own self
key_terms.لَا تَكِلْنِي: Do not leave me / Do not consign me

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of being 'left to oneself' in Shia supplications and how does it relate to Yunus ibn Matta?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) emphasizes the fragility of human spiritual state by citing Prophet Yunus (Jonah), whose brief moment of self-reliance—being 'left to his own self'—led to destruction despite not constituting major disbelief (kufr). This highlights the Shia scholarly distinction between minor spiritual negligence and outright apostasy, urging constant divine reliance (tawakkul) to prevent the soul from drifting into ruin.
